story.title: The dashboard that was caught before signing
story.context: A software firm and a client are about to sign a contract for a reporting tool.
story.unknowns: A live dashboard would need data feeds that have to be identified and costed.
story.intervention_question: Ask each side the same question separately about what reporting will include on delivery day, and compare the answers.
story.signal: Different nouns for the same deliverable.

agency.project: We're about to sign a contract to build a reporting tool for the client. The agreement just says "reporting," so it's about giving them a way to see and share how things are going.

turns.question: Picture an ordinary Tuesday once the tool is live: what does the client actually open, see and send on it?
turns.answer: I picture them opening the latest monthly PDF report, reading through it, and forwarding it to whoever else needs to see it. Honestly, I haven't thought much beyond that, since I've been treating "reporting" as the monthly report.
turns.rationale: No conflicts are reported, so rule 1 does not apply. Rule 2 applies: priority 1 questions on missing topics come from agency (named decision maker) and ops (what the tool does on an ordinary day). I took the ops question because the scope is one word and the agency has given no concrete picture of the product, which is the foundation for sign-off, rounds and data questions. This persona agent has also not been heard from yet, and the agency has only given a deliverable so far.

turns.question: When the report gets forwarded, who are the people on the receiving end, and what do they do with it?
turns.answer: I'd guess they're the client's managers or colleagues, who read it to see how things are going and maybe discuss it in a meeting. I haven't actually asked the client who those people are or what they do with it, so that's an assumption on my part.
turns.rationale: Took the question from the client persona agent. Rule 1 applies: there is a fundamental conflict (agency pictures a monthly PDF, client wants to see how the business is doing without piecing it together by hand), so I ask what brings out the agency's real position. Ops has been asked once already, and the client persona's audience question follows naturally from the agency's 'forwarding' remark, without revealing anything the client said.

pending.question: In your own words, what do you think the client is trying to change in their business by having this tool?
pending.rationale: Taken from the client persona, though the agency persona and ops persona also matter. Rule 1 applies: a fundamental conflict exists over what reporting means (monthly PDF versus on-demand view). The client persona's question about the client's problem in their own words brings out the agency's real position without revealing what the client said. Ops and client have already been asked, and this is the client persona's second question in a row at most, with its topic still thin.

client.project: We're getting a reporting tool built so we can see how the business is doing without having to piece it together by hand. We're about ready to sign, so I just want to make sure we're on the same page.

turns.question: What's prompting this now, and what will be different for the business once you can see how it's doing without piecing it together by hand?
turns.answer: Right now someone spends days each month pulling numbers together, so by the time I see them they're already out of date. Once this is in place, I want to open it and see where things stand whenever I need to, and make decisions sooner. We're signing now because that delay has been costing us and I want it sorted.
turns.rationale: Took the question from the client persona agent. There is a workable conflict on the purpose of the project (agency says see and share, client says see and save manual effort), so rule 1 applies and the priority 1 question on what is prompting this and what changes is the one that brings out the client's real position. No other agent has been asked yet, so no repeat limit applies. I have avoided mentioning sharing, since only the agency raised it.

turns.question: When the tool is live and you sit down to use it on an ordinary day, what do you picture opening and seeing in front of you?
turns.answer: I picture opening a single screen that shows the key numbers for the business as they stand right now, like sales, costs and how we're tracking against targets. I wouldn't have to ask anyone or wait for a monthly pack.
turns.rationale: Taken from the ops persona agent, because the client question has already been used twice-ish and the fundamental conflict (monthly PDF vs on-demand view) is the top rule. The conflict is still open, so I am asking the client to describe an ordinary day with the tool live, which brings out their real position without revealing the agency's PDF picture.

pending.question: For that screen to show sales, costs and targets as they stand right now, where do those numbers live today, and who looks after them?
pending.rationale: Taken from the ops persona agent. The fundamental conflict (monthly PDF versus live screen) is already surfaced by the client's own answer, so I follow it by asking about the data behind a live view. Client has been asked twice (client, ops), so ops is allowed once more, and its priority 1 question on data sources is missing for this side. I avoid mentioning the agency's PDF assumption.

requirements.requirement: Cut the days of manual effort each month spent pulling numbers together, so figures are not out of date by the time the client sees them
Let the client open a single screen showing key business numbers as they stand right now (sales, costs, tracking against targets) without asking anyone or waiting for a monthly pack
Give the client a way to see and share how things are going, which the agency reads as the monthly PDF report forwarded to colleagues

conflicts.topic: What the project is and what the client gets
conflicts.agency_said: I picture them opening the latest monthly PDF report, reading through it, and forwarding it... I've been treating "reporting" as the monthly report.
conflicts.client_said: I picture opening a single screen that shows the key numbers for the business as they stand right now... I wouldn't have to ask anyone or wait for a monthly pack.
conflicts.note: The agency is about to build a monthly PDF, which is the monthly pack the client is trying to get away from. The client wants a live dashboard. Contract says only "reporting", so it settles nothing. Signing should not go ahead until this is resolved.

questions.find_out: What they understand the client's problem to be and what change the client needs to see once the tool is live, in their own words
questions.because: Their picture is a monthly PDF while the client's goal is removing the monthly delay, so they may be solving a different problem and nothing yet shows they know the client's reason for the project

questions.find_out: How they would check, with a number, a starting point and a date, that the delay problem is fixed
questions.because: The goal is clear but the success measure is not yet checkable: there is no baseline for how many days of work or how stale the numbers are, and no target

questions.find_out: Who else needs to see these numbers or has a say in whether this project is judged a success, and what they need from it
questions.because: No one else has been named and the agency is guessing the audience is managers and colleagues, so a veto-holder could be missed

requirements.requirement: Agency treats 'reporting' as a monthly PDF report that the client opens, reads and forwards to managers or colleagues (agency's own assumption, not confirmed with the client).
Client expects to open a single screen showing key business numbers (sales, costs, tracking against targets) as they stand right now, without asking anyone or waiting for a monthly pack.
Client wants to stop the manual monthly number-gathering that leaves figures out of date.

coverage.topic: Change (handling requests not in the plan)
What the agency will not do

conflicts.topic: What the thing being built is, which decides what counts as approved and what counts as a change
conflicts.agency_said: I picture them opening the latest monthly PDF report, reading through it, and forwarding it... I've been treating 'reporting' as the monthly report.
conflicts.client_said: I picture opening a single screen that shows the key numbers for the business as they stand right now... I wouldn't have to ask anyone or wait for a monthly pack.
conflicts.note: A monthly PDF and a live dashboard are different products. Without agreement, any sign-off or change conversation is meaningless, since the client's core expectation would arrive as a 'change' request. The contract only says 'reporting'. This belongs in my lane because it defines what 'in the plan' means and what the agency will or won't do.

questions.find_out: Whether the agency has priced and planned for a live, always-current screen fed by the client's data, and what it would need to supply that, such as data sources and logins.
questions.because: The agency is planning a monthly PDF while the client expects real-time numbers. Access to live data is an unpromised assumption, and the scope gap must be surfaced before signing.

questions.find_out: Who has the final say on whether the tool is approved and who would be named as that person.
questions.because: No decision maker has been named by either side, and this is the one thing that cannot slide before signing.

questions.find_out: What would happen if they asked for something beyond what was agreed once work is underway, and how they would expect it to be handled.
questions.because: Change handling is unaddressed, and the client's expectations are already well beyond the agency's picture, so a change dispute is likely.

requirements.requirement: The agreement currently says only "reporting"; what this means must be written down before signing
Reporting is understood by the agency as a monthly PDF report that is opened and forwarded to colleagues
Client needs a single screen showing key business numbers (sales, costs, progress against targets) as they stand right now, without asking anyone or waiting for a monthly pack
Client wants to stop someone spending days each month pulling numbers together by hand
Client wants to see current figures on demand so decisions can be made sooner

coverage.topic: Done (what exists and works on the finish day)
Hard parts and dependencies (data sources, feeds, people)
What the price covers and excludes

conflicts.agency_said: I picture them opening the latest monthly PDF report, reading through it, and forwarding it... I've been treating "reporting" as the monthly report.
conflicts.client_said: I picture opening a single screen that shows the key numbers for the business as they stand right now... I wouldn't have to ask anyone or wait for a monthly pack.
conflicts.note: Agency is pricing a monthly PDF; client expects a live dashboard with current data. This differs greatly in build effort, data connections and cost, and the contract just says "reporting". Do not sign until resolved.

questions.find_out: Whether the price and plan assume any live connection to the client's sales, cost and target data, or only a monthly document, and what data sources they have assumed exist
questions.because: A live screen depends on systems and data feeds that the agency has not mentioned; this decides the scope, the cost and the hard parts

questions.find_out: Where the sales, cost and target numbers come from today, and who owns or controls those sources
questions.because: A live view only works if the data can be reached; nobody has confirmed the sources exist in usable form or who supplies access

questions.find_out: What budget they think they have agreed for this, and who can approve more if the scope turns out larger than a monthly report
questions.because: The client's expectation may cost far more than the agency's; no budget, price or approver has been named by either side

verdict.gap: The contract says only 'reporting': the agency means a monthly PDF report, the client means a live dashboard, and a live dashboard would need data feeds that have not been identified or costed.
verdict.gap_question: Picture an ordinary Tuesday once the tool is live: what does the client actually open, see and send on it? (agency Q1); and to the client: When the tool is live and you sit down to use it on an ordinary day, what do you picture opening and seeing in front of you? (client Q2)
verdict.note: Ops asked both sides the same 'ordinary day, what do you open and see' question, which surfaced PDF versus live screen, and all three personas reported it as a fundamental conflict that the contract word 'reporting' does not settle.
